english_draft: Preview: No prior preview was available. Analysis: For the quarter ended June 30, 2026 (calendar Q2 2026, Microsoft FY2026 Q4), Microsoft reported revenue of $90.0 billion, up 18% (17% constant currency). Operating income was $40.6 billion, up 18%. GAAP net income was $35.8 billion, up 31%; non-GAAP net income was $35.3 billion, up 22%. Diluted EPS was $4.81 GAAP and $4.74 non-GAAP, up 32% and 23%, respectively. Microsoft Cloud revenue was $59.3 billion, up 27%. Commercial remaining performance obligation rose 84% to $678 billion. Several discrete items produced a net benefit of $0.27 per diluted share versus the forward-looking guidance of April 29, 2026. These included a $3.2 billion gain from the Anthropic investment and lower-than-expected Voluntary Retirement Program expenses, partly offset by Xbox severance expenses and impairment charges. Management said revenue, operating income, and diluted EPS exceeded expectations after adjusting for these items. Segment results: Productivity and Business Processes revenue was $37.8 billion, up 14%; Intelligent Cloud revenue was $39.3 billion, up 32% (31% constant currency), with Azure and other cloud services up 43%; More Personal Computing revenue was $12.9 billion, down 4% (5% constant currency). Within MPC, Windows OEM and Devices revenue fell 7%, Xbox content and services revenue fell 10%, and search advertising excluding traffic acquisition costs rose 10% (9% constant currency). Microsoft returned $10.2 billion to shareholders. The release did not provide quantitative guidance for the next quarter. There was no prior preview to review.
